capabilities: Navigate a structured graph neighborhood around the current note (Compass, Mind Map, Facets views)
Create, reclassify, unlink and hide Parent, Child, Friend, Challenger, Previous and Next relationships
Filter and restyle the canvas with Quick Filter and Graph Lenses
Edit notes beside the graph in a companion Sidecar pane or embedded editor node
Import ontology and styling from classic ExcaliBrain
extras: README carries an explicit warning that the plugin is new and may modify relationships, recommending backups and testing on a small note set first; development is funded via Ko-fi and a downloadable sample Help vault is provided.
intentEvidence: K-Plex uses its own plugin ID, so you can keep ExcaliBrain installed while migrating your settings.
motivation: The author built it because large graph views become dense and hard to navigate, and wanted a structured neighborhood that works as a day-to-day surface for moving through notes rather than staring at the entire vault.
problem: Obsidian's graph view renders the whole vault as a dense force-directed layout where connections have no consistent spatial meaning, making it hard to reason about the current note's relationships.

relations.evidence: If classic ExcaliBrain is installed and running, K-Plex can import its ontology and graph, node and link styling.
optional Excalidraw note creation when Excalidraw is installed
Plain Markdown, core template variables and supported Templater code are processed before relationship properties are written.

summary: Ontology-driven graph navigator that shows a structured neighborhood of the current note (parents, children, friends, challengers) on an interactive canvas.
